rescue.fts_lostsignal.title: Rescue frequency 145.500
rescue.fts_lostsignal.no_station: You need to be at a radio station.
rescue.fts_lostsignal.no_power: The radio station has no power.
hide.fts_lostsignal.hidden: You are under the bed. Keep still. Crouch to come out.
hide.fts_lostsignal.out: You come out from under the bed.
hide.fts_lostsignal.no_room: There is no room beside the bed to get under it.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SEE_SIGN: Wait. There's a sign on a tree. It's got this frequency on it, and an arrow.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SEE_TRAIL: I found a trail! I think it's a trail. It's like a path.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SEE_TOWER: I can see a tower! A wooden tower, up on the hill. Is that you?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SEE_LIGHT: I can see a light. Up high. Is that your light?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SEE_CLIFF: There's a drop. Like, a cliff. I can't go down this way.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SEE_LAKE: I can see a lake, off to the side.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SEE_RIVER: There's a river. A big one. I don't think I can cross it.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SEE_CREEK: I can hear water. There's a creek, just below me.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SEE_SNOW: There's snow up here. A lot of it. My feet are soaked.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SEE_RIDGE: I'm up on a ridge. It's really windy up here.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SEE_TREES: I'm in thick trees. Pines, I think. I can't see much of anything.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SEE_ROCKS: Just rocks. Big grey rocks everywhere.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SEE_MEADOW: I'm in a meadow. Open grass. Some flowers.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SEE_NOTHING: I don't know. Trees. Everything looks the same.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_TIRED: I need to stop for a minute. I'm so tired.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_DARK: It's getting really dark. I don't want to walk in the dark.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_COMPASS_YES: Yeah, I've got a compass. On my pack.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_WHICH_WAY: Which way? I can't tell which way is which out here.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_OK_01: Okay. Okay, I'll head that way.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_NO_WATER: I can't hear any water. Not from here.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_NO_TRAIL: I don't see a trail anywhere.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_NO_SIGN: There's no sign here. Just trees.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_FOLLOW_SIGN: Going the way the arrow points.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_NO_LIGHT: I can't see any light from here.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_STAY: Okay. I'll stay right here. Please don't forget about me.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_FLARE: Lighting a flare now. Can you see it? Over.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_FLARE_NONE: I'm out of flares. That was my last one.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_FIRE: I made a little fire. Can you see the smoke?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_LAMP: My lamp's on. I'm waving it.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_LAMP_DAY: In broad daylight? You'd never see a lamp from up there. I could make smoke.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_CALL_01: Hello? Is anyone on this channel? Over.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_CALL_02: Hi, um... I think I'm lost. I saw this frequency on a sign on a tree. Is anyone there?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_CALL_03: Hello?! Anyone? Please, I need help. Over.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_CALL_04: This is... I'm a hiker, I left the trail and now I can't find it. It's getting dark.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_AT_TOWER: I'm at the bottom of your tower. Can I come up?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SEE_YOU: I can see you! Over here! Over here!
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_FOUND: Good work up there, Lookout. Real good work. District out.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_LOST_CONTACT: Lookout, District. We lost contact with your hiker. If you hear anything, anything at all, call it in.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_FEAR_STANDIN: It's... it's just standing there. It's not moving. Why isn't it moving?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_FEAR_RUN: Oh no. Oh no no no...
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_GO_LOOK: Lookout, District. Nothing from your hiker since last night. We need eyes where they called from. Go in daylight, take your radio, and be back before dark. Over.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_BODY_FOUND: ...Copy. Copy that. We'll send people up for them. Come back to the tower, Lookout. Now, please. District out.
radio.fts_lostsignal.note.where: District's note: last heard from about %2$s blocks %1$s of your tower (bearing %3$s°).
remains.fts_lostsignal.found: It's %s. You take the journal from their jacket.
remains.fts_lostsignal.again: %s. There is nothing more you can do here.
journal.fts_lostsignal.start:
Day one.

Parked at the trailhead by 7. Weather's perfect. Planning to make the ridge by noon and camp by the lake. Two days, easy.

Brought the little radio Dad made me take. Feels silly.
journal.fts_lostsignal.lost:
Lost the trail somewhere after the creek. Kept thinking it'd show up again over the next rise.

It didn't.

Everything looks the same. Found a sign nailed to a tree with a radio frequency on it. 145.500. Who puts those up?
journal.fts_lostsignal.answered:
Someone answered! A lookout, up in a tower somewhere. Kind voice. Told me what to look for and which way to go.

Getting dark too fast. Stopped for the night like they said. Fire's going.

I'm going to be fine.
journal.fts_lostsignal.unanswered:
Called on the radio over and over. Nothing. Just hiss.

Made a fire. Ate the last of the bread.

Once I thought someone answered, but when I asked who it was, it just repeated what I said. My own voice. Must be an echo or something.
journal.fts_lostsignal.last:
someone is standing
in the trees

it doesnt move when
i look at it

it was closer
the last time i looked

keep the fire up
keep the fire
finder.fts_lostsignal.ring: Fire finder: %s° %s. Hold the sight steady on a signal; crouch to step away.
finder.fts_lostsignal.read: Reading taken. The way back is in the rescue panel.
finder.fts_lostsignal.away: You step away from the fire finder.
finder.fts_lostsignal.reading: Fire finder: %1$s at %2$s° (%3$s), about %4$s blocks. Bearing back to the lookout: %5$s°.
rescue.fts_lostsignal.last_reading: Last reading: %1$s at %2$s°, about %3$s blocks. Walk back on %4$s°.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_THANKS_01: Thank you. Thank you so much. I really thought... thank you.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_ON_TRAIL: I'm on the trail now. I think I can make it down from here. Thank you, Lookout.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_01: You know what the forest does with a fallen tree? It makes a hundred new ones.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_02: Everything up here grows back. It just needs something to grow from.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_03: A fire looks like ruin. Then spring comes, and the ground is grateful.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_04: The forest doesn't hate anyone. It only keeps the ones who forget whose house this is.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_05: Every season the mountain takes a little back. It's only fair. We take so much.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_06: You built your tower very high. Higher than the trees. They notice that kind of thing.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_07: Nothing is wasted in the woods. Nothing.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_08: Rot is just the forest remembering.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_09: You watch the trees all day. Have you ever wondered what the trees watch?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_10: People come up here to get away from something. The mountain asks what they brought with them.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_11: A wolf isn't cruel. A storm isn't cruel. Why do we only call it cruel when it's a man?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_12: There's a balance up here. Someone has to keep it. You keep the fires.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_13: The ground is patient. It has never been hungry for long.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_14: When the snow comes, everything is forgiven. Everything is covered.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_15: They put up signs so people don't get lost. As if the mountain wants them found.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_SAY_16: The old ones planted with their own hands. And gave back with them, too.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_HELLO_01: Afternoon. Beautiful up here, isn't it?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_HELLO_02: Oh. I didn't mean to startle you.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_ASK_01: That's your tower up there? All on your own?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_ASK_02: Does anyone know you're up here? Family? Anyone at all?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_ASK_03: How long have you been up here? You start to hear things, don't you.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_KNOWS_01: You're the one on the radio at night. You have a kind voice.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_KNOWS_02: The fellow at the other tower. He doesn't answer anymore, does he?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_WATER: Could I trouble you for a little water?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_WATER_THANKS: Thank you. I'll save it for later.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_BYE_01: I'll see you around. The mountain is smaller than it looks.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_BYE_02: Get home before dark. It's a long way down.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_DOOR_01: It's cold out here. You have a warm room. That's all I'm asking for.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_DOOR_02: I saw your light from the valley. Let me in.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_DOOR_03: You don't have to be afraid of me. I'm just a man.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_DOOR_04: I can wait. I'm very good at waiting.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_RADIO_01: Yes, I'm here. Everything's fine. Everything is fine up here.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_RADIO_02: He went down for supplies. He'll be back. You could come and wait with me.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_RADIO_03: No smoke tonight. Nothing burning. Not yet.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_QUIET: Quiet day. Hot. Nothing on the horizon.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_WEATHER: Weather's turning. Rain by tonight, I'd say.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_SAW_MAN: Saw a guy on the ridge trail this morning. No pack, no water. Didn't wave back.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_SAW_LIGHT: There's a light in the tower across the valley. Nobody's posted there. Is anybody posted there?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_HEARD_WHISTL: Heard whistling below the tower last night. Three short ones. Then it stopped.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_NEED_COAL: My generator's running dry. If you're heading down, I could use some coal.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_NEED_CHECK: Haven't heard from the next tower over since yesterday. Could you swing by when it's light?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_SMOKE: I've got that smoke too. Crossing your bearing now.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_NIGHT: Lock up tonight. Don't open for anyone. I mean anyone.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_CHATTY: You ever notice how quiet it gets right before dark? Like everything's holding its breath.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_NERVOUS_01: Sorry. I'm jumpy. I haven't been sleeping.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_NERVOUS_02: Someone was at my door last night. I didn't open it. I didn't open it.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_HELLO: Oh! Hey. Didn't hear you come up. Want some coffee?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_STAY_YES: Stay if you want. Honestly, I'd be glad of the company.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_STAY_NO: You can't stay the night. Sorry. Just... get home before dark.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_MET_HIM: A man came up the stairs yesterday. Asked for water. Never drank it.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_CHECK_TOWER: Lookout, we haven't heard from a tower in your area since yesterday. If you can get eyes on it in daylight, do.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_TOWER_EMPTY: Copy. We'll mark it. ...Lock your door tonight, Lookout.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_NOBODY_POSTE: Lookout, nobody's posted at that tower this season. Say again what you heard?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_SMOKE_CROSS: Copy both bearings. We've got a fix. Crew's on the way. Good eyes.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_SUPPLY: There's a supply crate at the trailhead for you. Pick it up in daylight.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_NEW_KEEPER: Heads up, Lookout. We've got someone new posted across the valley. Say hello.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_HURT_01: I fell. My ankle... I can walk, but slow.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_HURT_02: I think it's broken. I can't put any weight on it.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_COLD: I'm so cold. I can't stop shaking.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_REPLY_01: Oh thank God. Okay. Okay. Hi.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_REPLY_02: You can hear me? Okay. Good. That's good.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SAY_AGAIN: Sorry, say again? You're breaking up.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_STEEP: It's too steep. I can't get down here, I'll fall.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_WATER: The water's too fast. I'm not crossing that.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_FREEZING: It's freezing. I can't feel my hands.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_HURT: Ow, ow... I think I twisted my ankle.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_BATTERY: My battery's getting low. I don't know how long this radio's gonna last.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_CAMP: I'm gonna stop here for the night. I'll call you in the morning.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_FEAR_WHISTLE: Did you hear that? Someone whistled. Was that you?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_FEAR_FOLLOW: Something's following me. I can hear it walking when I walk.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_FEAR_VOICE: It said my name. How does it know my name?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_FEAR_NOT_YOU: That wasn't you. On the radio. That wasn't you, was it?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_SOMEONE: There's someone here. A man. He's... he's just smiling at me.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.H_HE_SAYS: He says he can show me the way down. Should I go with him?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_MORNING_02: Morning, Lookout. Loud and clear. Have a good one. District out.
tower.fts_lostsignal.state.abandoned: the door's open, and no one there.
tower.fts_lostsignal.state.stranger: no one's posted there, but someone has been living in it.
call.fts_lostsignal.heading: Call
call.fts_lostsignal.no_answer: No answer from Lookout %s. Only static.
talk.fts_lostsignal.title: %s, Lookout %s
journal.fts_lostsignal.keeper_start:
Week three.

Quiet. Two smokes, both lightning, both out by noon. Saw elk on the north slope.

The generator eats more coal than they said it would.
journal.fts_lostsignal.keeper_man:
There's a man who walks the ridge trail without a pack. Today he stood at the foot of the tower for an hour and looked up.

When I waved, he waved back. Slowly. Like he was copying me.
journal.fts_lostsignal.keeper_last:
He came up the stairs tonight.

He says he only wants to talk. He says the mountain is owed. He says it kindly.

I'm not opening the door. I'm not
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.X_YOUR_VOICE: [your own voice, as if off a tape]
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_WHO_01: Lookout, District... say again? We didn't send anyone up there tonight.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_WHO_02: Lookout... who are you talking to? That channel's been quiet all night.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.R_CALL: Hello. Is anyone on this channel. Over.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_MORNING_01: Lookout, District. Morning radio check, over.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_WEATHER_01: Lookout, District. Send me your weather when you're ready. Over.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_WEATHER_02: Copy your weather. Thanks, Lookout. District clear.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_EVENING_01: Lookout, District. End of day check. All quiet up there? Over.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_EVENING_02: Copy that. Get some rest. District out.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_NIGHT_RULES: Lookout, District. Standard reminder: after dark you stay in the cab. Door shut, lamp lit. Don't go out for anything you can't see. District out.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_OVERDUE_01: Lookout, District. We have a hiker overdue in your area. Keep an ear on one-four-five point five tonight. Over.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_OVERDUE_02: Lookout, District. Got a call from a family, their kid didn't come down off the mountain. Keep listening, over.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_CHECK_NIGHT: Lookout, District. Just checking in. You there? ...Lookout?
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_SMOKE_01: Copy your smoke. We'll get a crew out there. Good eyes, Lookout.
fire.fts_lostsignal.read_first: Take a bearing on the smoke with the fire finder first, then call it in.
fire.fts_lostsignal.crossed: Lookout %s crosses it on %s°. The District has a fix.
supply.fts_lostsignal.where: The crate: about %s blocks %s of the tower's foot, where the trail starts up.
hiker.fts_lostsignal.title: %s, lost on the mountain
district.fts_lostsignal.said.D_MORNING_0: District, Lookout %s. Loud and clear, over.
district.fts_lostsignal.said.D_EVENING_0: District, Lookout %s. All quiet up here, over.
rescue.fts_lostsignal.static: static, a voice somewhere in it, too faint to make out
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_HIDE_YES: Okay. Okay. Under the bed. Don't make a sound.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_HIDE_NO: I'm not crawling under a bed in my own tower.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_HIDE_DAY: Hide? From what? It's broad daylight.
journal.fts_lostsignal.start.1:
Day one.

Took the long loop because the short one was closed for a washout. Map says nine miles to the lake. Map also says the trail is maintained.

Packed too much food. Better than too little.
journal.fts_lostsignal.start.2:
Day one.

First trip alone in years. Promised Mom I'd text from the top. No signal past the second switchback, which is sort of the point.

The air up here smells like pencils.
journal.fts_lostsignal.start.3:
Day one.

The ranger at the trailhead asked if I had a radio. I said yes. She said good, and wrote down my car's plate.

Why would she need the plate.
journal.fts_lostsignal.lost.1:
The trail just stops at a rockslide. I went around it high, and when I came down the other side there was no trail.

I've walked back to the rocks twice. They don't look like the same rocks.
journal.fts_lostsignal.lost.2:
Fog came in after lunch. Couldn't see ten feet. Kept walking downhill, because downhill is where people are.

When it lifted I didn't recognize anything. Not one thing.
journal.fts_lostsignal.lost.3:
Followed what I thought were trail markers. Little cuts in the bark, at head height.

They went on for a mile and then they went in a circle. I don't think people made them.
journal.fts_lostsignal.answered.1:
Got someone on the radio. A lookout. They asked what I could see, and I described rocks and trees like an idiot, and they said that was fine, that helps.

They sound tired. I'm not alone out here. I keep saying that to myself.
journal.fts_lostsignal.answered.2:
The lookout answered on the third try. Told me to stay put and keep a fire smoking.

I did. Before dark I could almost see the tower on the ridge. A light came on up there. Somebody is watching for me.
journal.fts_lostsignal.answered.3:
Talking to the lookout makes it better. Flat, calm voice, like a pilot's.

They said the District knows about me. They said in the morning. Morning is eleven hours away.
journal.fts_lostsignal.unanswered.1:
Nobody on the radio. I said my name and where I parked, in case someone is listening and can't answer.

Battery's at half. I'll try again at dark. Saving it.
journal.fts_lostsignal.unanswered.2:
Tried every hour. Just the hiss.

Around nine a voice said hello. When I answered it said hello again, exactly the same, like a recording.

I turned the radio off. Then I turned it back on.
journal.fts_lostsignal.unanswered.3:
No one answers. I found the sign with the frequency again, or another one just like it.

The nails in it are new. Bright. Somebody put it up this week.
journal.fts_lostsignal.last.1:
it walked around the fire
all night
just outside the light

when i call the lookout
it stops to listen

it knows what a radio is
journal.fts_lostsignal.last.2:
theres a man
he says hes the lookout
he says follow him down

but the lookout
sounded different

didnt they
journal.fts_lostsignal.last.3:
he knows my name
i never said it out loud
only on the radio

he was listening
hes been listening
the whole time
journal.fts_lostsignal.keeper_start.1:
Day nineteen.

Rain all week. The rain gauge overflowed twice. Nothing burns in this, which is the only good thing about it.

Radio check every morning. District sounds like they're reading it off a card.
journal.fts_lostsignal.keeper_start.2:
Week five.

The hiker from over by the next tower came out at the trailhead, safe. Felt good about that for a whole day.

Out of coffee. Out of patience with the generator.
journal.fts_lostsignal.keeper_man.1:
Found boot prints on the stair this morning. Up to the walkway, around once, back down. I was asleep.

Nobody's boot prints but mine should be on that stair.
journal.fts_lostsignal.keeper_man.2:
The man from the trail asked me for water today. I gave him a bottle. He held it the whole time he talked and never drank.

He asked how many nights I've been up here alone. I told him. I don't know why I told him.
journal.fts_lostsignal.keeper_last.1:
District doesn't answer. The other towers don't answer.

He's knocking. Three, then nothing, then three.

If you find this, I didn't open it.
journal.fts_lostsignal.keeper_last.2:
He's been at the window. Not the door. The window.

He's smiling at me like he's waiting for me to remember something.

Going under the bed. If he
journal.fts_lostsignal.night.weather.cle: Clear and cold. So many stars. I hate how quiet it is.
journal.fts_lostsignal.night.weather.rai: Raining. Everything I have is wet.
journal.fts_lostsignal.night.weather.thu: Thunder all evening. Every flash, I see the trees for a second.
journal.fts_lostsignal.night.weather.sno: Snowing. My tracks fill in behind me.
journal.fts_lostsignal.night.place: I told the lookout what I could see: "%s"
journal.fts_lostsignal.night.no_place: I couldn't tell anyone where I am. I don't know where I am.
journal.fts_lostsignal.night.order: The last thing they told me: "%s." That's what I'm doing.
journal.fts_lostsignal.night.no_order: Nobody has told me anything. I'm staying by the fire.
journal.fts_lostsignal.night.whistle: Someone whistled out in the dark. Three short ones. Not a bird.
rescue.fts_lostsignal.handheld: On your handheld: five watts, not far, and not through a mountain.
rescue.fts_lostsignal.pmr: A PMR walkie-talkie can't be set to 145.500. It takes a ham transceiver.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_QUAKE: Lookout, District. We had a quake reported in your area. Everyone all right up there? Any damage to the tower? Over.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_QUAKE_02: Copy. Glad you're in one piece. We'll get someone up to look at those legs when we can. District out.
district.fts_lostsignal.said.D_QUAKE: District, Lookout %s. Shook hard, but we're standing. Over.
rescue.fts_lostsignal.lost: Lost? Call a lookout round you: its keeper puts a flare up to walk towards, and takes a bearing on yours.
guide.fts_lostsignal.way: Lookout %1$s has you on the finder: you are about %2$s blocks %3$s of it. Walk on a bearing of %4$s° (%5$s).
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_LOST_FLARE: Okay. Hang on. I'm putting a flare up from the tower. Watch for it, and walk towards it.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_LOST_LAMP: And I've lit the lamp. As long as you can see that light, you walk towards it.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_LOST_ASK: If you've got a flare, put one up. I'll get a bearing on you from here.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_LOST_ASK_NIG: If you've got a flare, put one up. Or swing a lantern, up high. I'll get a bearing on you from here.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_LOST_SEEN: There you are. I've got you on the finder. Walk the bearing I'm giving you, and you'll see the tower before long.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.K_LOST_NOT_SEE: Didn't see a thing. You must be behind a ridge from me. Get up somewhere high and try again.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_LOST: I see you. Don't move. Stay right where you are, and I'll come down to you.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_LOST: District. If you've lost your way out there, call the nearest lookout on this frequency. Put up a flare if you've got one. They'll find you from the tower.
radio.fts_lostsignal.line.D_POSTED: Lookout, District. Welcome aboard. You're posted at this tower for the season. Your terminal and your handbook are coming up with the next supply run. District out.
desk.fts_lostsignal.new_mail: LOOKNET: new message on your terminal (%s unread)
desk.fts_lostsignal.posted: You are posted at Lookout %s for the season. Your terminal and handbook come up with the next crate, at the foot of the trail.
desk.fts_lostsignal.closed: The lookouts are closed for the season.
desk.fts_lostsignal.dark: The screen is dark: no power. Is the station's generator running?
desk.fts_lostsignal.off: This terminal is switched off in this world's settings.
desk.fts_lostsignal.mail.welcome.subject: POSTING: LOOKOUT %s

desk.fts_lostsignal.mail.welcome.3: Pay is weekly, in credit: %1$s for each day on duty, %2$s for each duty done, and more for good work. Spend it on page 5; orders come up with the next morning's crate.

The season is closing. Stay sharp to the end; the last dry spell is the worst.

handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.name: Lookout Guide
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.1:
LOOKOUT GUIDE

Cold Fork Ranger District

Reprinted 1994, with the LOOKNET supplement.

Keep this book in the cab.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.2:
1. YOUR JOB

You are the eyes of the District. Watch the country, report smoke at once, take the weather at 1300, answer the radio checks, and keep the cab in order.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.3:
2. THE DAY

0700 radio check
1300 fire weather
1730 end of day check
Dusk: walkway lamp lit

Between times, sweep the horizon with the fire finder.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.4:
3. THE FIRE FINDER

Stand at the finder and sight along it. Hold it steady on the smoke and read the bearing off the ring. Judge the distance by the country between.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.5:
4. REPORTING SMOKE

Give the bearing, the distance, and what the smoke is doing: colour, shape, size. On the terminal: SMOKE. On the radio: Report smoke.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.6:
5. FIRE WEATHER

At 1300 read the instruments yourself: temperature, humidity, pressure and its tendency, wind and where it comes from, rain since midnight, the sky.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.7: Type what you read. Do not guess. The District checks your figures against the instruments and will send them back to be read again. Careful readings are paid for.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.8:
6. THE RADIO

One-four-five point five. Say who you are and who you call. Over: your turn. Out: done. Keep it short; others are waiting.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.9:
7. SUPPLIES

A crate comes to the foot of your trail every few days. Order what you need on the terminal against your pay credit; it comes the next morning.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.10:
8. PAY

You are paid weekly, in credit: for each day on duty, each duty done, and for good work. The slip comes to your terminal.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.11:
9. AFTER DARK

Stay in the cab. Keep the door shut and the walkway lamp lit. Do not go out for anything you cannot see.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.12:
10. LOST PEOPLE

Keep them talking. Find out what they see. Have them signal: a flare, smoke, a lamp at night. Take a bearing and walk them in.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.13:
11. LOST YOURSELF

Call the nearest lookout on your handheld and put up a flare. They will take a bearing on you and tell you the way.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.14:
LOOKNET

The terminal runs off the station's power. If the generator stops, so does the terminal. Number keys turn the pages, Tab moves between fields, Enter sends.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.page.name: Folded Page
handbook.fts_lostsignal.page.1:
If you're reading this you got my old book. Some things they don't print.

If he knocks, three and then three, don't answer. Get under the bed. Don't make a sound.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.page.2:
Watch him. He won't come while you watch. He comes when you look away.

A tower nobody's posted at that says everything is fine is not fine.

Three whistles is help. Two or four is him.

C.
lightning.fts_lostsignal.warning: The radio crackles. A hum from the roof, and your hair stands on end.
lightning.fts_lostsignal.struck: Struck: the tower took the lightning, and you with it.

desk.fts_lostsignal.mail.gear.1: Coming up with the next crate: a fire danger sign for the foot of your trail, a lightning stool, and the new edition of the guide.
desk.fts_lostsignal.mail.gear.2: Set the sign to the morning's rating each day. In a lightning storm, stand on the stool.

desk.fts_lostsignal.eval.days: Days on duty: %1$s. Duties done: %2$s%% of the roster.
desk.fts_lostsignal.eval.work: Fires called in: %1$s. Hikers brought in: %2$s. Observations right in full: %3$s.
desk.fts_lostsignal.eval.close.a: Exemplary. We want you back next season, on the same tower if you'll have it.
desk.fts_lostsignal.eval.close.b: Good work. You're welcome back next season.
desk.fts_lostsignal.eval.close.c: Adequate. Next season, keep to the roster.
desk.fts_lostsignal.eval.close.d: We need lookouts who are at their towers. We'll talk before next season.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.15:
12. LIGHTNING

A lookout on a summit is struck. In a lightning storm stand on the glass-footed stool. If the rod hums and glows blue, get on it now.
handbook.fts_lostsignal.guide.16:
13. FIRE DANGER

Each morning the District rates the day's fire danger from yesterday's 1300 figures. Set the sign at the foot of your trail to match.
letter.fts_lostsignal.name: Letter from %s
letter.fts_lostsignal.1.1:
Dear Lookout %3$s,

It's %1$s. You won't remember my voice, but I remember yours. You got me down off that mountain.
letter.fts_lostsignal.1.2:
I got to my car the next day. My mother cried for an hour. I keep thinking about how you didn't give up on me.

Thank you, %2$s.

%1$s
letter.fts_lostsignal.2.1:
To the lookout at %3$s,

This is %1$s, the hiker from that night. I'm home. My feet are a mess, but I'm home.
letter.fts_lostsignal.2.2:
There's something in with this. It isn't much. I wanted you to have something from me.

I'll come up to see the tower next summer. In daylight.

%1$s
letter.fts_lostsignal.3.1:
%2$s,

They told me your name at the ranger station, and I wrote it down so I'd never forget it. That night I was sure nobody would come.
letter.fts_lostsignal.3.2:
Somebody did. I still dream about the trees sometimes. Then I remember you finding me, and I wake up fine.

With love,
%1$s

desk.fts_lostsignal.map.name: District map (Lookout %s)
marion.fts_lostsignal.intro.subject: night desk
marion.fts_lostsignal.intro.1: hey. marion, night desk. you'll see my name a lot after dark.
marion.fts_lostsignal.intro.2: if you can't sleep i'm here till six. coffee's terrible. how's %1$s?
marion.fts_lostsignal.intro.r2: who else is up at this hour?
marion.fts_lostsignal.intro.a1.1: wind's good. wind means you hear things coming.
marion.fts_lostsignal.intro.a2.1: me, the repeaters, and whatever's walking the ridge. kidding. mostly.
marion.fts_lostsignal.obs.subject: your 1300
marion.fts_lostsignal.obs.1: saw your 1300 come through. clean numbers. somebody down here noticed.
marion.fts_lostsignal.fire.subject: good eyes
marion.fts_lostsignal.fire.1: heard you call in that smoke. crews love a lookout who gives them a distance.
marion.fts_lostsignal.fire.r2: do you get a lot of them?
marion.fts_lostsignal.fire.a1.1: it's always only smoke. until it isn't.
marion.fts_lostsignal.fire.a2.1: every dry week. this district had twice the towers once. then the budgets.
marion.fts_lostsignal.rescue.subject: a phone call
marion.fts_lostsignal.rescue.1: the hiker you brought in. their mother called the desk this morning to say thank you.
marion.fts_lostsignal.rescue.2: i cried in the bathroom. don't tell anyone.
marion.fts_lostsignal.knock.subject: last night
marion.fts_lostsignal.knock.1: you hear anything at your door last night?
marion.fts_lostsignal.knock.a1.2: keep it shut. i mean it. whatever it says.
marion.fts_lostsignal.knock.a2.1: no reason. keep it shut anyway.
marion.fts_lostsignal.corinne1.1: i used to be up there, you know. ninety-six. lookout 47.
marion.fts_lostsignal.corinne1.a2.1: somebody had to sit down here. so nobody's alone on the radio.
marion.fts_lostsignal.corinne2.subject: corinne
marion.fts_lostsignal.corinne2.1: corinne had 48, the next ridge over. we talked every night. she had a laugh that carried on the radio.
marion.fts_lostsignal.corinne2.2: one night she said someone was at her door. calm, polite. like he knew her.
marion.fts_lostsignal.corinne2.a1.1: don't open it. i said it twice.
marion.fts_lostsignal.corinne2.a1.2: in the morning her door was open and she was gone.
marion.fts_lostsignal.corinne2.a2.2: there should be a word for knowing a report is wrong.
marion.fts_lostsignal.page.subject: her handwriting
marion.fts_lostsignal.page.1: you've got an old guide up there? one with a folded page in it?
marion.fts_lostsignal.page.2: that's her handwriting. i'd know it anywhere. keep it. do what it says.
marion.fts_lostsignal.hollow1.subject: hollow peak
marion.fts_lostsignal.hollow1.1: ever hear of hollow peak? closed in seventy-nine. there was a fire. three men died.
marion.fts_lostsignal.hollow1.a1.1: the lookout saw the smoke two days before and said nothing. that's the official version.
marion.fts_lostsignal.hollow1.a2.1: because you're up there. and i'm tired of being the only one who remembers.
marion.fts_lostsignal.hollow2.subject: arthur
marion.fts_lostsignal.hollow2.1: the hollow peak lookout was arthur lund. he had his boy up there every summer. silas.
marion.fts_lostsignal.hollow2.2: arthur walked into the woods that winter. in the spring they found the boy in the tower. alone.
marion.fts_lostsignal.hollow2.a1.1: sixty, if he's alive. nobody knows. or nobody says.
marion.fts_lostsignal.hollow2.a2.1: i think you know why it matters.
marion.fts_lostsignal.last.subject: end of season
marion.fts_lostsignal.last.1: last night of the season. you did good up there.
marion.fts_lostsignal.last.2: come back in the spring, okay? and lock the door on your way out.

radio.fts_lostsignal.line.S_THANK_BURN: Thank you for letting it burn.

costs.fts_lostsignal.burned.body: A fire burned itself out in your area today and nobody called it in. What happened, Lookout?
marion.fts_lostsignal.fake.subject: two a.m.
marion.fts_lostsignal.fake.1: were you talking to someone on the radio at two last night?
marion.fts_lostsignal.fake.2: it wasn't me. i was on all night and heard nothing from you but static.
marion.fts_lostsignal.fake.r1: they asked if i was alone.
marion.fts_lostsignal.fake.a1.1: don't ever answer that. i call you by your name. if it says lookout and not your name, it isn't me.
marion.fts_lostsignal.fake.a2.1: maybe. keep the door shut anyway.
